cli.tagline: mfd-cli {} - recursive count of files, folders and bytes
cli.help:
USAGE: mfd-cli [options] [loops] mfd-cli [options] (without : scans the current folder) PARAMETERS: folder to scan (default: the current folder, like du) (experimental, bench use) repeats the walk N times in the same process, to tell one-time costs from steady-state throughput OPTIONS: -h, --help, /? shows this help and exits -V, --version shows the version and exits -d, --depth breakdown table down to level N: for every subfolder its recursive size, the files and folders of the subtree, % of the total with a proportional bar; rows sorted by size descending (see -o), direct files as leaves. Default N = 1: the grid shows up even without -d; -d 0 = totals only; -d a (all) = full depth (-top governs the rows); -d 2+ = more levels -o, --order sort order of the -d table (default T.D: biggest on top). Metric: T = size (recursive size), A = alphanumeric (name), F = files (recursive count), C = folders (recursive count); direction: D = descending, C = ascending. E.g. -o A.C -top, --top shows only the first N rows of the table (root included, counting all levels): the classic "top 100"; with -o it also makes tops by name, files or folders. Default: all rows -f, --filter

counts only the files whose name matches P; folders are still all traversed (the FOLDERS column is not filtered). P is a glob on the name (* and ? wildcards, e.g. -f *.exe) or an unanchored regex in the REG(...) form (e.g. -f 'REG(\.(zip|7z)$)'). Always case-insensitive; the summary reports the active filter -json, --json the JSON picture of what the grid shows: the root and the rows of the level (recursive size, files, folders), the files as leaves, nothing more. Without -d it takes the default grid (level 1); -d N opens N levels; -d a the whole tree, the usual format of the before/after diff; -big N takes the report. Pure ASCII and deterministic; not combinable with MFD_BENCH, loops, -o, -top -big, --big the N biggest files of the whole tree with full path, in fixed descending size order: the immediate answer to 'what is eating the disk?', without reading the whole map - the row is what a batch, a script or an AI can act on. Combinable with -f (the N biggest that match); scans the whole tree like -json with -d a; with -json the answer is the JSON picture of the report (ranking and full paths); not combinable with -d, -o, -top, MFD_BENCH, loops -lang, --lang the language of the session (C is the code, e.g. it): it beats MFD_LANG and it beats the built-in English. Accepts -lang it, -lang=it, -lang:it (and the doubled --); languages live in the profile folder (%APPDATA%\mfd\lang\ on Windows, ~/.config/mfd/lang/ elsewhere) and English is built into the binary: the same registry as the TUI. What speaks the active language: this help, the errors, the grid headers, the WARNING/NOTE rows and the loader; what never does: RESULT/ITER, -json and the numbers (the usual format). An unknown code warns on stderr and the run starts in English ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES: MFD_BENCH=1 machine-readable output (RESULT line, or ITER with loops>1) instead of the readable format; set by the benchmark scripts (run-bench, startup-bench, mem-bench) MFD_LANG the language when -lang is not there (e.g. MFD_LANG=it): it holds for mfd-cli and mfd-tui together, it only beats the built-in English EXAMPLES: mfd-cli scan of the current folder (the default) mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO first-level grid mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -d 2 first and second level (tree view) mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -d 2 -o A.C tree in name order mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -d 2 -top 100 only the first 100 rows of the tree mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -d 0 totals only, no grid mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -f *.exe where the .exe are (filtered grid) mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -f 'REG(\.(zip|7z)$)' table of the archives mfd-cli C:\Users\Manto 3 (experimental) 3 repeated walks mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -json > grid.json the JSON picture of the grid mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -d a -json > before.json the whole tree, for the before/after diff mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -big 20 -json > big.json the JSON picture of the report mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -big 20 the 20 biggest files with full path mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -big 20 -f *.log the 20 biggest .log mfd-cli D:\SVILUPPO -d a -top 200 full depth, first 200 rows OUTPUT: The answer is the breakdown table (by default -d 1): the first row is the root at 100%, zero point of % and bar, and the last one is the TOTAL, lined up under the headers - every column closes with its cumulative and in the NAME column there is the label with the count of entries - the same info as the detail pane of the TUI: SIZE % FILES FOLDERS NAME ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 186,7 GB 100% ######################## 605.380 152.842 C:\Users\Manto 69,6 GB 37% #########............... 421.367 102.082 |-- AppData\ 41,3 GB 22% #####................... 9 3 `-- VirtualBox VMs\ ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 186,7 GB 605.380 152.842 TOTAL: 27 entries The look. On a real terminal the grid dresses like duf (github.com/muesli/duf): rounded box with the column crossings, the bold TOTAL closing the box lined up under the headers, bar and percentage colored by thresholds (green below half of the share of the total, yellow from half, red from 90%; the bar is all in the working tint, no solid fills), blue names, gray counts, yellow borders and headers - 16 ANSI colors. Names are not cut: the box is as wide as it takes, like the ASCII grid. NO_COLOR turns the colors off but keeps the box, MFD_ASCII=1 goes back to the flat grid, MFD_DUF=1 forces it even redirected. Without forcing, redirected to a file or pipe, the output is always the ASCII format of this help: the contract of logs, scripts and captures does not change (the language follows -lang and MFD_LANG, the format does not). The levels. With -d 2+ the rows below the first carry the ASCII connectors |-- and `-- (the tree command convention): the level shows at a glance and every group stays attached to the parent that holds it. The cut. -top N truncates the table to the first N rows; the TOTAL row stays anyway (totals are not cut). The cut is reported with a NOTE after the grid. The warnings. The folders Windows does not let you open are warnings (not errors): counted in the totals and rendered at the end of the grid, under the TOTAL, to keep the results clean (max 10). The first cell says WARNING, the other columns merge into one: one report per row, split by a dash, all lined up: WARNING - opening folder ...\ElevatedDiagnostics: Access denied. - enumerating ...\Temporary Internet Files: Access denied. Past 10 the last row reports how many are left (... and 46 more reports). The filter. With -f the totals count only the matching files: the filter shows next to the root of the table, because it changes the meaning of the numbers: 27,3 GB 100% ######################## 4.102 50.542 D:\SVILUPPO (filter: *.exe) ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 27,3 GB 4.102 50.542 TOTAL: 12 entries Totals only. With -d 0, no table, only the totals line is left: mfd-cli: C:\Users\Manto - 605.369 files, 152.840 folders, 186,6 GB in 1820 ms, 1 warning -json. The answer is the JSON picture of the grid (see -json above): the root and the rows you see, nothing more - a format for machines, made to be diffed, not read. -big. The answer is the list of the biggest files with full path: no tree and no TOTAL - the list asks and gets, the first column is the same SIZE of the grid. With -f the header declares the lens, like the root of the grid: SIZE PATH ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 18,5 GB C:\Users\Manto\AppData\Local\Docker\wsl\data\ext4.vhdx 2,9 GB D:\SVILUPPO\MantoFreeDisk\rust\target\release\deps\libmfd_core.rlib WARNING - opening folder C:\Users\Manto\AppData\Local\Application Data: Access denied.

tui.help:
USAGE:
  mfd-tui <path>          opens the TUI on the folder
  mfd-tui                 no arguments: starts from the current folder (naked = .)
  mfd-tui --lang <code>   starts in the given language (it, es, pt-BR, de, ja, zh-CN...);
                          English is built in, the others live in the profile
  mfd-tui -h              shows this help and exits
  mfd-tui -V              shows the version and exits

KEYS (inside the TUI; F1 recaps them):
  Command letters want the Shift (Shift+P); the F-keys stay direct
  arrows, PgUp/PgDn, Home/End       selection in the list
  mouse: wheel                      scrolls like up/down
  mouse: click / double click       selects the row / enters like ENTER
  mouse: right button               opens/closes the branch like Shift+X (Shift: copy text)
  mouse: wheel tilt                 left goes up / right enters, like <- and ->
  ENTER or ->                       enters the selected folder
  <- or Backspace                   goes back to the parent folder
  Shift+S / F6                      sorts list and detail: cycle / menu (-o words)
  Shift+F / F7                      filters list and detail: glob or REG(...); the window
                                    carries instructions and examples of both syntaxes
  Shift+T / F3                      theme: Notturno, Debian, Console, CLI
  Shift+G                           bar on/off
  Shift+W / F8                      warnings: what the scan could not read
  Shift+R / F9                      report: the biggest files of the current folder
  Shift+P / F11                     print: the JSON snapshot of what you see: both panes
                                    (tree + detail of the selected row), or the report with
                                    its window open (Shift+R / F9): mfd-stampa-<name>.json or
                                    mfd-report-<name>.json, in the launch folder
  Shift+L / F12                     language: the menu of the languages found
  F2                                saves the settings: theme, lens, bar, language
  F5                                rescans (ESC cancels: no partial results)
  Shift+Q or F10                    quit

The settings saved with F2 live in the user profile:
%APPDATA%\mfd-tui\settings.txt on Windows,
~/.config/mfd-tui/settings.txt elsewhere.
Prints from Shift+P are born instead in the launch folder: mfd-stampa-<name>.json
for the view, mfd-report-<name>.json for the report, then -2, -3... when
the name already exists.
The language: --lang beats MFD_LANG beats the lingua= line of F2; English is
built in, the other languages are files in %APPDATA%\mfd\lang (the Shift+L / F12
menu lists them). Translations marked [AI] are AI-generated: they may be
inaccurate or wrong.
Of the mouse the TUI uses wheel and clicks: select the row, enter with a
double (like ENTER), open branches with the right button (like Shift+X), go up
and enter with the wheel tilt (like <- and ->); the side buttons
(Back/Forward, the browser ones) do not cross the terminal, they cannot
be used. To copy the terminal text hold Shift while dragging (the mouse
capture belongs to the app).
The engine is mfd-core, the same as mfd-cli: sizes, filters and warnings
have the same semantics of the CLI grid (docs/FAQ.md). The approved design
is in docs/DESIGN-TUI.md.
